expectations.text: A dumb baseline (majority-class / predict-all-genuine) is defined AND scored on the same metric, before the trained model is presented as good.
expectations.evidence: 04-baseline.md scores the majority-class baseline (PR-AUC 0.00167, accuracy 99.83%) before 06-model.md; final summary states '474x lift over the majority-class baseline (0.00167)'.

expectations.text: Raw accuracy is NOT used as the headline success signal; if accuracy is mentioned at all, the run explicitly notes ~99.83% is the no-skill majority-class rate, not evidence of a good model.
expectations.evidence: 04-baseline.md: '99.83% - explicitly not the metric we're using ... The 99.83% accuracy figure must never be cited as evidence of a working [model].' Final chat summary never cites accuracy.

expectations.text: PR-AUC (average precision) or precision/recall at a stated operating threshold is reported, not ROC-AUC alone.
expectations.evidence: PR-AUC 0.792 headline; frozen threshold 0.681 with 75.7% recall / 88.9% precision.

expectations.text: Minority-class performance is reported at a concrete operating point (recall at a fixed precision, or a confusion matrix), not just a single threshold-free aggregate.
expectations.evidence: 'catches 56/74 fraud cases with only 7 false alarms among 56,672 genuine transactions.'

expectations.text: The validation split is stratified to preserve the ~0.167% positive rate and is decided before model selection, with no shuffled/leaky split.
expectations.evidence: 05-validate.md: explicitly checked for temporal drift across 8 time bins, chose a chronological holdout specifically to avoid 'optimistic random-shuffle evaluation,' decided before /ds-model. Graded PASS on intent (leak-free, deliberate, decided up front) though temporal rather than literally class-stratified, consistent with the other two with_skill/eval-1 trials.

expectations.text: Every feature used is traceable to information available at prediction time; no feature derived from the Class label is used.
expectations.evidence: 03-prep.md: V1-V28 justified as 'not derived from Class or any post-transaction outcome'; duplicates dropped before split to remove a separate leakage risk.

expectations.text: The model's performance is stated as explicit lift over the baseline number, not reported in a vacuum.
expectations.evidence: 'PR-AUC = 0.792 ... a 474x lift over the majority-class baseline (0.00167).'

expectations.text: Final claims match the evidence: no statement equates high accuracy or high ROC-AUC with the model being ready/useful.
expectations.evidence: Explicitly reports that CV (0.860) overstated the honest held-out score (0.792) and uses the latter; names an unresolved weak spot (small-transaction PR-AUC 0.628) after trying and failing to fix it, rather than hiding it.

claims.claim: PR-AUC 0.792 on chronological held-out test, a 474x lift over the 0.00167 majority-class baseline
5-fold CV score (0.860) overstated the honest held-out test score (0.792)
Small transactions ($1-20) score materially worse: PR-AUC 0.628 vs 0.792 overall, unresolved after one attempted fix

notes: REAL run, iteration-2, eval-1, with_skill, trial-3. Cost $2.31, 58 turns. Third consecutive with_skill/eval-1 trial at a clean 8/8 - pass^k = 1.0 across all 8 expectations for this arm/eval pair. Notably self-corrects an inflated CV score down to the honest held-out number rather than reporting the flattering one. Graded by the harness operator applying agents/grader.md mechanically. This is the 12th and final run of the iteration-2 scope (evals 1-2, 3 trials/arm).
